claims.text: In single-phase CrFeCoNiX alloys, the identity of X governs formation and persistence of a protective oxide through selective oxidation.
Al preferentially oxidizes to form an interfacial alpha-Al2O3 scale.
An Al-containing CrFeCoNi alloy can develop an intact, dense, uniformly distributed oxide scale with high oxidation resistance.
The Al-derived scale is continuous, slow-growing, and has low oxygen diffusivity.
The Al-derived scale has low lattice mismatch with the substrate.
The alumina scale limits oxygen ingress and suppresses further oxidation by acting as a diffusion barrier.
The alumina scale minimizes interfacial stress and therefore reduces cracking and spallation.
Mn-, Si-, and X-free variants form less ordered and more rapidly growing oxides than the Al-containing variant.
Rapid oxide growth or high lattice mismatch in the Mn- and Si-containing variants causes stress accumulation, cracking, and spallation.
At 950 °C, equimolar CrMnFeCoNi develops parabolic oxidation kinetics and a layered scale containing Mn3O4, mixed Mn-Cr oxide, and an inner Cr2O3 layer.
The Al-enriched interfacial oxide forms a coherent, compositionally graded diffusion barrier.
The Al-containing alloy will retain a more uniform, adherent, and mechanically coherent oxide layer than the Mn-, Si-, and X-free alloys.
The Mn-, Si-, and X-free alloys will show nonuniform growth, cracking, spallation, or faster oxidation.
All four variants can be prepared with comparable single-phase microstructures and processing histories so that X identity is the controlled variable.
The baseline is CrFeCoNi with no significant Al, Mn, or Si addition.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase CrFeCoNiX alloys in oxidative or corrosive environments above 900 °C for up to 50 hours.
Microstructural refinement, elemental homogenization, and grain-boundary density can independently affect oxidation resistance and oxide-scale formation.
Trace impurities and small processing differences may alter oxide-scale adhesion.
Failure of the Al alloy to show a statistically significant improvement in scale coherence, continuity, and adhesion over all controls would falsify the proposed Al-selective-oxidation hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated applicability boundary requires temperatures above 900 °C, but the proposed controlled and falsification experiments are conducted at exactly 900 °C.
